# Does it qualify? USMCA origin with a bill of materials

Narration script (110 s). Edit video/v4-usmca-origin-bom/script.yaml and rebuild.

## title

- Does this pump qualify for USMCA? Check its bill of materials.

## why

- A valid claim under the US-Mexico-Canada Agreement earns the preferential duty rate.
- A wrong one means a duty bill later: be ready to prove it.
- We test criterion B: it meets its product-specific rule.

## rule-bom

- Fictional pump PK-100 is made in Mexico from this bill of materials.
- Its rule: a change of heading into eighty-four AA, or regional value content, RVC.
- Sixty percent by transaction value, or fifty by net cost.

## steps12

- Step one, list the non-originating: motor, housing, fasteners, seventy-eight dollars.
- Step two, the tariff shift: each needs a different heading from the pump's.
- Motor and fasteners pass; the housing shares heading eighty-four AA and fails.

## deminimis

- Step three, de minimis: failing parts are allowed up to ten percent of the value.
- Fourteen over two hundred is seven percent: the pump qualifies, criterion B.

## whatif

- Now the housing costs twenty-five: de minimis is eleven point eight percent, fails.
- Step four, RVC by transaction value: fifty-seven point eight percent, fails.
- By net cost: fifty-one point nine percent, qualifies.
- Net cost is the producer's data, so the producer or exporter normally certifies.

## document

- Step five, document: the bill of materials, certifications and the calculation.
- Add the rule text, who checked, and the date.
- Then issue or accept the certification and set the flag in our system.
- When customs verifies, this file is what you produce.

## remember

- The rule is tested on the bill of materials; the file proves the claim.
- Next: customs primer section ten and Anki Units two and three.
